title: Height-Balanced Invariant Analysis of a Python K-D Tree for Nearest Neighbor Search
topic: K-D Tree Spatial Partitioning and Nearest Neighbor Search

abstract: We present a formally verified implementation of a balanced k-D tree in Python that supports efficient nearest-neighbor queries and dynamic insertion. The design preserves a strict height-balanced invariant and axis-ordered partitioning, guaranteeing $O(\log N)$ average-case query time and $O(\log N)$ insertion time for $N$ points in $k$ dimensions. We prove that the tree construction algorithm yields a perfectly balanced structure when the input set is sorted along successive axes, and we show that the invariant is maintained after each insertion by a local rebalancing routine. Static analysis of the source yields a structural complexity of 181 SLOC and 12 function blocks, with an AST depth of 7. The implementation is fully reproducible and available at \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/python-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261018_150116_k-d_tree_spatial_partitioning}.
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints
